sentences.text: This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 21.09.2011 passed by Member, III rd Additional MACT, District Gwalior, (in short "Claims Tribunal") in MACC No.40/2010 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation and also aggrieved by the finding given by the Claims Tribunal by exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of injury of the claimant, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,48,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest @ 7% per annum from filing of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16812 2 MA-26-2012 claim petition till its realization.
Liability has been imposed upon the owner of the offending vehicle.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Claims Tribunal has committed grave error in awarding the amount and totally exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.
Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation firstly to the claimants and then, it may be recovered from the owner/respondent No.2 of the offending vehicle.

It is further submitted that compensation Smt.Kesharbai vs Dharmendra Kumar on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119156780/
1 awarded by the Claims Tribunal accepting inadequacy, assessed income of deceased Rs.3,000/- per month, which is on lower side and submitted that compensation must be assessed Rs.3995/- as per Minimum Wages Act.

sentences.text:
It is further contended that accepting the earnings of deceased as Rs.3995/-
per month and adding future prospect, applying adequate multiplier, a reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
Hence, learned Claims Tribunal has awarded the compensation on lower side, therefore, it is prayed that compensation amount be enhanced and just and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company contended that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no enhancement.
He supported the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record it is undisputed that at the time of alleged accident, driver of the alleged vehicle driving the heavy vehicle but he had only LMV licence, not valid and effective licence.

So, in light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. 2019 (2) MPLJ NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16812 3 MA-26-2012 (SC) 8, it is held that the Insurance Company shall be liable to make payment of the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner.

sentences.text: So, finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal with regard to totally exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability, is not correct in the eye of law.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record, in the considered opinion of this Court, just and proper income of the deceased would be according to the Minimum Wages Act, must be Rs.3995/- per month.

8. In view of aforesaid, the compensation awarded by learned Claims Tribunal is modified to the extent indicated under:-
 Heads Compensation awarded.
 Income Rs. 3995/- PMx12=Rs.47940/-
 Future prospects 40% Rs. 19,176/- per annum  Dependency Rs.67,116 (47940+19176) X 1/2

Total Income Rs. 7,25,044/-
 Enhancement Rs.4,77,044/- ( Rs. 7,25,044  Smt

2 9.
The learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.2,48,000/-.
Thus, the claimants are held entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.4,77,044/- (Rs.7,25,044/- - Rs. 2,48,000/-) in additional.
A ccordingly, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.

The amount of compensation is enhanced to lump sum amount of Rs.4,77,044 /- in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal, making total compensation amount of Rs.7,25,044/- payable by the Insurance Company to the extent that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:16812 4 MA-26-2012 Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the alleged vehicle.
10. The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said compensation amount be paid by the Insurance Company within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
With the aforesaid modification, the appeal is partly allowed and stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
